what: A task held back for 0.09 GiB made the daemon drop reth's whole kept front end (about 55 GiB held of a limit of 67.08 GiB); the next build, a one-line revert, took 195.4 s where it takes 4 to 16 s. The same code had been patched twice before for single cases (the room between two ledger turns, a whole-ceiling task) and the rule itself stayed.
cost: 195 s on the next edit of every checkout each time it fires; a third lane on the same decision
cause: the driver had one answer to any memory wait: every kept front end, whole, in the loop turn that saw the wait, before the purge asked in the same step had landed
whys: why wrong: 55 GiB of the dearest thing the daemon holds went for a 0.09 GiB wait
why possible: Jobs::let_go took no amount and no cost; Plane::short's number was only compared with 0
why not caught: each earlier fix removed one way for `short` to be non-zero and left what happens when it is
why easy: letting go of everything is one loop; a give-back in order needs a measure between steps, which nothing owned
property: a decision with one action, taken on a predicted number, in the same turn as the cheaper remedy was only asked for
class: an all-or-nothing remedy for a graded need
prevention: blaze_graph::giveback::Planner is the one rule (order, proportion, floor, hold, measure between rungs), with a simulation whose control is the old behaviour; a `Give` carries a `Planned` mark only the planner can make, and the driver drops a front end for memory only on a `Give`; the existing guard bound `let_go` (no `kept front ends let go for memory` span on a warm edit) still counts the same span and log line
fix: crates/blaze-graph/src/giveback.rs and crates/blaze-cargo/src/serve/job/giving.rs (written, not compiled: write-only lane)
state: written on int-1112, not compiled or run
